html:
The voyage on which the Portuguese captain Diogo Cão reached the mouth of the Congo River in 1482 or 1483. It opened ties between Portugal and the Kingdom of Kongo.

Sent by King John II to push further down the African coast, Cão set up a stone pillar, a padrão, at the river mouth to mark the Portuguese claim. He sent men inland to the king of Kongo, the manikongo, and when they did not come back he took Kongo hostages to Lisbon. On a later voyage he returned them and pushed south to what is now Namibia.

The contact grew fast. In 1491 the Kongo king was baptised, and his son Afonso I made Kongo a Christian kingdom that wrote letters to Lisbon and Rome. The same link later fed the Atlantic slave trade. Cão's work set up the voyage of Bartolomeu Dias round the Cape of Good Hope in 1488.
sum: The voyage on which the Portuguese captain Diogo Cão reached the mouth of the Congo River in 1482 or 1483. It opened ties between Portugal and the Kingdom of Kongo.
